learningObjectives.title: Mineral requirements: nitrate and magnesium ions

questions.q: Which word equation correctly represents photosynthesis?
questions.explain: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen using light energy.

questions.q: Which is the correct balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Six molecules of carbon dioxide and six of water yield one glucose molecule and six of oxygen.

questions.q: What two things are required for the reaction of photosynthesis and are usually written above the arrow in the equation?
questions.explain: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, which drives the conversion of the raw materials into glucose.

questions.q: What is the main role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
options: It absorbs light energy for the reaction
It supplies carbon dioxide to the leaf
It stores glucose made in the leaf
It transports water into the cells
questions.explain: Chlorophyll traps light energy and transfers it to chemical energy in the products of photosynthesis.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, energy is transferred from which form to which form?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose molecules.

questions.q: Photosynthesis is best defined as the process by which plants:
options: Manufacture carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water using light energy
Break down glucose to release energy for cells
Absorb mineral ions from the soil through roots
Lose water vapour through the stomata
questions.explain: Photosynthesis makes carbohydrates from raw materials using energy from light absorbed by chlorophyll.

questions.q: When testing a leaf for starch, which result shows that starch is present?
questions.explain: Iodine solution changes from orange-brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.q: In the starch test, why is the leaf boiled in ethanol before adding iodine?
options: To remove the chlorophyll so colour changes can be seen
To kill the cells and stop reactions
To soften the waxy cuticle for gas exchange
To add starch back into the leaf
questions.explain: Ethanol dissolves out the green chlorophyll, decolourising the leaf so the iodine colour change is visible.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists three limiting factors of photosynthesis?
options: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature
Nitrate ions, magnesium ions and light
questions.explain: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature can each limit the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is meant by a 'limiting factor' of photosynthesis?
options: A factor in short supply that restricts the rate of the reaction
A factor that is always present in excess
A factor that stops photosynthesis permanently
A product that slows the reaction as it builds up
questions.explain: A limiting factor is the one in shortest supply, holding back the rate even if others are plentiful.

questions.q: On a graph, the rate of photosynthesis rises as light intensity increases, then levels off and stays constant. What does the flat (plateau) region show?
options: Another factor, such as carbon dioxide or temperature, is now limiting
Light intensity is the only factor limiting the rate
questions.explain: When the rate no longer rises with more light, a different factor has become the limiting one.

questions.q: A grower raises the temperature of a greenhouse far above the optimum and the rate of photosynthesis falls. Why?
options: Carbon dioxide is completely used up
questions.explain: Very high temperatures denature the enzymes controlling photosynthesis, so the rate falls.

questions.q: Nitrate ions are needed by a plant mainly for the production of:
questions.explain: Nitrogen from nitrate ions is used to make amino acids, which are joined to form proteins.

questions.q: Magnesium ions are required by a plant for the production of:
questions.explain: Magnesium ions are an essential component needed for making chlorophyll.

questions.q: A plant grown without magnesium ions develops yellowing leaves. What is the best explanation?
questions.explain: Without magnesium the plant cannot make chlorophyll, so leaves turn yellow (chlorosis).

questions.q: A farmer notices crops with stunted growth and poor protein content, though the leaves are still green. Which mineral ion is most likely deficient?
questions.explain: A shortage of nitrate ions limits amino acid and protein synthesis, causing stunted growth.

questions.q: Which leaf tissue contains the most chloroplasts and is the main site of photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells near the upper surface are packed with chloroplasts for maximum photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is the main function of the stomata in a leaf?
options: To allow gases to diffuse in and out of the leaf
To transport sugars around the plant
To absorb mineral ions from the soil
To store starch made in the leaf
questions.explain: Stomata are pores, controlled by guard cells, that allow carbon dioxide in and oxygen out for gas exchange.

questions.q: What is the function of the waxy cuticle on the upper surface of a leaf?
options: To reduce water loss from the leaf
To exchange gases with the air
To store water for the plant
questions.explain: The waterproof waxy cuticle reduces evaporation of water from the leaf surface.

questions.q: How does a leaf being broad and thin help it carry out photosynthesis efficiently?
options: A large surface area absorbs light and gases can diffuse a short distance
It reduces the amount of light absorbed by the leaf
It prevents any water from entering the leaf
It stops carbon dioxide reaching the mesophyll
questions.explain: A broad shape captures more light while thinness gives short diffusion distances for gases.
